analyst_view.overall: Early view: two teams on nine points chasing a top-eight place. Barcelona beat Aston Villa 3-0 and then won 2-1 at Atlético on Sunday to stay top in La Liga, while Manchester City won 3-2 at Leipzig but lost at Nottingham Forest at the weekend and Marc Guéhi has since withdrawn from the England squad. Rodri's hamstring injury was expected to keep him out for about a month from 3 November, so he may just be back.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals. I lean a little lower: Barcelona kept a clean sheet against Villa, and a meeting of two top-eight contenders in December is often tighter than either side's results against weaker teams. Barcelona's 14 goals and Haaland's form still make three or more likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, almost evenly split. I see no reason to move it: both teams attack through wingers (Yamal and Raphinha, Doku and Foden) but prefer to work the ball into the box rather than win corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean a little higher: the top-eight places are on the line for both, and fast wide players on each side (Yamal, Raphinha, Doku) tend to draw tactical fouls when the game opens up.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, which looks low next to their 4.3 goals. I lean higher: Barcelona have scored 14 in four games and City 12, and with neither side likely to defend deep, both should get well over ten attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. That matches two very good attacks, so I keep it. If Guéhi's injury keeps him out, City's defence could give up more clear chances than expected.
